answer: Cross-Epoch Identity Drift Scoring. An agent's response and timing patterns are hashed into a rolling fingerprint each epoch; a new identity must keep its fingerprint consistent across at least three consecutive epochs before its actions count toward rewards. The tide of incoming clones cannot reset the clock cheaply, since maintaining many agents through that warm-up consumes real compute on genuine tasks. Identities failing the drift check are barred at the wharf, so an attacker pays full operating cost per clone for several epochs before any pearl of reward is reachable.
